text:
Alex: Quick follow-up from today's RFC check-in — proposing a minimal control-plane gateway that only handles auth/handshake and then punts data-plane to customer's endpoint. Thoughts?
Maria: I like the isolation idea. main question: who owns TLS termination for mutual auth? gateway or endpoint?
Sanjay: prefer gateway do mTLS for identity proofing, then forward a short-lived connection token to endpoint. avoids exposing KMS creds to tenant infra.
Kevin: concern: double TLS handshake adds latency. if gateway terminates then re-establishes to endpoint we add ~20-50ms per connection in some regions. can we do TLS passthrough with SPIFFE identity?
Maria: SPIFFE passthrough is neat but requires sidecars or proxies in private envs that understand our certs. ops footprint increases.
Lisa: ops perspective: fewer long-lived IP mappings is better. ephemeral client IPs + NAT on our side will blow up support tickets. we need predictable egress IPs for customers that use allowlists.
Alex: proposal: three-mode gateway: 1) mTLS-terminate-and-tokenize (default), 2) TLS-passthrough (when tenant sidecar present), 3) relay (when endpoint unreachable). choose based on tenant capability flag.
Sanjay: that matches earlier routing policy idea. we should pick mode at handshake based on tenant profile + per-request policy. store capability flags in tenant config-service.
Kevin: rollout notes: we must measure handshake latency, token issuance errors, and percent connections falling back to relay. add metrics: cp.handshake.ms, cp.token.fail_rate, cp.fallback.relay_pct.
Alex: agreed. ops-bot can we add dashboards?
ops-bot: Created dashboard "CP Gateway Handshake" with charts cp.handshake.ms (p95/p50), cp.token.fail_rate, cp.fallback.relay_pct. link: https://dashboards.internal/r/gw-handshake
Lisa: runbook for fallback: if fallback.relay_pct > 5% for 5m -> check endpoint health, check NAT limits, check tenant capability mismatch. escalation to networking oncall after 10m.
Maria: security checklist: 1) token TTL <= 60s, 2) sign tokens with per-region KMS keys, 3) audit logs containing token issuance and gateway IP.
Sanjay: implementation note: prefer ephemeral UDP hole-punching for keepalive? jk. seriously though, prefer TCP keepalive + periodic refresh to avoid cold starts in low-throughput tenants.
Kevin: sample handshake pseudocode I sketched:
```
client -> gateway: ClientHello + tenant-id
gateway verifies tenant config
if mode == TERMINATE:
  gateway mTLS auth client
  issue short_token
  gateway -> endpoint: connect using token in ALPN header
elif mode == PASSTHROUGH:
  tunnel raw bytes
else:
  fallback to relay
```

Lisa: compatibility: we need a migration path for tenants using allowlist of our EGRESS IPs. option A: reserve per-tenant egress pool (expensive). option B: provide static relay endpoints per-region for allowlists.
Alex: option B seems cheaper operationally. we can offer dedicated relay endpoints as an enterprise SKU.
Maria: migration/canary plan: enable PASSTHROUGH for 10 internal tenants, 50% traffic, monitor cp.handshake.ms and auth failure rate. then open to customers with sidecar installed.
Sanjay: testing: unit tests for token TTL, integration tests simulating network partition and relay fallback, chaos tests for certificate rotation.
Kevin: docs TODO: one-pager on modes, sequence diagrams, and sample sidecar config. I'll take docs.
Lisa: ops TODO: runbook, alert thresholds, and mapping table of tenant -> gateway mode. I'll own runbook.
Alex: Security TODO: finalize token format and KMS rotation window. Maria?
Maria: on it. will propose token JSON + sig, plus short-lived reference IDs to avoid replay.
Kevin: anything else?
Sanjay: one more: we need to limit gateway resource usage per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors (conn limits, rate limits during handshake). add quotas in config-service.
Alex: good catch. quota entries and rate-limit errors should surface clearly to SDKs.
Lisa: thanks everyone. I'll draft rollout playbook and post here for review. :thumbsup:
